reporting.title: Report prohibited content
reporting.description: Report an unsafe AI-generated image, a prohibited edit, impersonation, or a rights violation to the EzImageAI operator. Anyone can report a concern; no account is required.

details.violation: Describe the suspected violation and why it concerns you. For infringement or impersonation, explain your connection to the affected work or person.
details.reference: Tell us when and where you encountered it. Include a job or asset reference, or a public page address, if available.
details.reply: Use an email address where the operator can reach you for clarification and the outcome. Put Content report in the subject.

reporting.safety: Do not send passwords, tokens, cookies, private signed media links, or unnecessary personal data. Do not download, attach, or forward suspected child sexual abuse material or other illegal content; describe it and provide an existing reference instead.
reporting.urgent: For child safety, terrorism, or imminent serious harm, put URGENT content report in the subject. Initial response: within 2 hours. Action completed: within 24 hours, including weekends. For immediate danger to life, also contact the appropriate emergency service.
reporting.process: The operator acknowledges, classifies, reviews, and acts on reports, then replies with the outcome where privacy and law allow. The content policy lists all four severity levels and handling times. If a review needs longer, you will receive the reason and an updated timeframe.
reporting.appeal: To challenge a decision, email the same address with Content appeal in the subject and explain the decision and any new evidence. Appeals receive a response within 10 business days.
reporting.policyLink: Read the content policy and all response times

conversion.title: Customer conversion and attribution
conversion.basis: An open funnel for customers registered in the selected period. Each stage counts distinct customers, excludes administrators, and is optional. Percentages use registrations as the denominator; they are not consecutive step conversion rates. Paid means verified production payment, excluding renewals.
conversion.traffic: Consented traffic in this period: {browsers} browser identifiers, {pageViews} page views.
conversion.coverage: Browser events cover {known} of {total} registered customers. {unknown} have unknown registration sources. {internal} internal browser identifiers excluded.
conversion.noObservations: No consented browser observations in this period. Click counts may be missing; historical visits cannot be reconstructed.
conversion.sourceBasis: Traffic uses observed acquisition source; customer outcomes use the source saved at registration. UTM takes priority over referrer. Missing history stays unknown. Browser identifiers last up to 30 days and are not people or GA sessions. Do not divide these traffic and registration counts as a conversion rate.
conversion.checkoutTitle: Checkout observations in this period (event counts, including visitors)
conversion.failureTitle: Failed generation jobs in this registration cohort
conversion.linkedVisitors: Of these observed browsers, {registeredBrowsers} are linked to a new server-confirmed registration ({rate}); {successfulBrowsers} later generated successfully and {paidBrowsers} have verified payment. This consented sample uses registration-hook evidence, not ordinary logins; unobserved journeys remain unlinked.
conversion.aggregateBasis: Hourly totals since {since} (UTC), filtered by time and device. Sources are broad categories; this summary always shows all sources independently of the detailed source filter above. No visitor identity or account linkage. These are page views, not unique people or a conversion denominator; repeat visits and unrecognized bots can remain.
conversion.generationBasis: Top 50 groups of permitted browser observations, not distinct users or confirmed jobs. Text length is a bucket; no input text or file contents are recorded.

experimentReport.title: Purchase experiments
experimentReport.activityBasis: Activity in this date range, split by registration before or during the range. Completion time is server creation to successful terminal state, not time to visible image. Views and download starts need optional analytics; missing observations are not proof of no use.
experimentReport.basis: Each experiment assigns consented browsers 50/50. First visible exposure within retained history starts a 7-day attribution window. Source/device filters apply to exposure. Only server-linked, unambiguous accounts can contribute checkout and verified production payment outcomes; renewals, tests and pre-exposure checkouts are excluded.
experimentReport.interpretation: Entry clicks measure the tested surface; control has no added result-guide button. Compare downstream checkout clicks and verified payments in both arms. Mature rates use only browsers with a full 7-day window. Small samples, consent gaps, ambiguous links and interaction between the two tests prevent declaring a winner from CTR alone.
